blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing logistics risk in practice means building a simple, live risk register and a very small number of rehearsed responses to the crises most likely to happen. Each risk is scored for likelihood and impact. Each has an owner. Each has a one-page response, so that when it happens, nobody is inventing a solution while the phone rings.

The register is not a document to admire. It is a tool the team updates as the world changes — a new border rule, a new strike, a new supplier problem — and refers to whenever something actually goes wrong. When the moment comes, the team pulls the page off the shelf, adapts it to the specific situation, and acts.

If we had not had a plan for the port strike in March, we would have spent the week inventing one. Instead, we spent the week executing. That is what risk planning buys you — not fewer crises, but calmer ones.

items.q: According to the text, what are the two dimensions used to score each risk?
items.why: "Each risk is scored for likelihood and impact."

items.q: What does the author say the register is NOT?
items.why: "The register is not a document to admire." — é ferramenta viva, não enfeite.

items.q: According to the text, what does risk planning actually buy you?
options: A guarantee that strikes will not happen
items.why: "not fewer crises, but calmer ones."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Every risk needs a named owner.
The register should change as circumstances change.
A risk register should be reviewed only once, when it is written.
A rehearsed response saves time in a crisis.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que o registro é vivo e atualizado "as the world changes" — o oposto de escrever uma vez só.

items.q: The March port strike example suggests that…
options: the team could have avoided the strike entirely
having a plan let the team act instead of improvise
items.why: Inferência: com plano, gastaram a semana executando; sem plano, teriam gasto inventando.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte reconstruindo o registro de riscos com a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, let's rebuild this properly. After the March strike, I don't want us ever again to be writing a response at eight in the morning with the port already closed. So here's how the new register works.

Every risk gets two scores — how likely it is, and how badly it would hurt us. High-likelihood, high-impact goes to the top. And every single risk gets one named owner. Not a team, not a department — one person who wakes up thinking about it.

For the top ten, I want a one-page response written now, while things are calm. What we do first, who we call, which supplier we switch to. When the crisis lands, we pull the page off the shelf, adapt it, and act. We are not inventing anything on the phone.

And this is the part people forget: the register is never finished. A new border rule appears, a new strike is announced, a supplier wobbles — we update it that week. If we had kept it live back in February, honestly, March would have been a much quieter month.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte say she never wants to happen again?
options: Having too many owners for one risk
Closing the port during a strike
Writing a response while the crisis is already unfolding
items.why: "I don't want us ever again to be writing a response at eight in the morning with the port already closed."

items.q: How many owners does Charlotte want per risk?
items.why: "one named owner. Not a team, not a department — one person."

items.q: When should the one-page responses be written, according to Charlotte?
options: After the crisis, as a review
items.why: "I want a one-page response written now, while things are calm."

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "the register is never finished"?
options: It must be updated continuously as new risks appear
It should be rewritten from scratch each year
It is too long to complete
items.why: Inferência: ela lista mudanças (nova regra, greve, fornecedor) e diz "we update it that week" — o registro é vivo.

items.q: Her closing remark about February and March implies that…
options: a live register would have made the crisis easier to handle
the strike would not have happened at all
the register should be paused in quiet months
items.why: Inferência (third conditional): "If we had kept it live… March would have been a much quieter month."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We keep a live risk register that the whole desk can see." A risk register is…
options: an organised record of risks, their scores and owners
a list of past accidents only
items.why: Risk register = registro de riscos: os riscos, suas pontuações e responsáveis, atualizados.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Because the response was ___ in advance, nobody panicked when the port closed."
items.why: Rehearsed = ensaiado: preparado e praticado antes, o oposto de inventar na hora.

items.q: "We score each risk from one to five." To score here means to…
items.why: To score = pontuar: dar um valor/nota ao risco.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The strike had low ___ but very high impact, so it went to the top of the list."
items.why: Likelihood = probabilidade: quão provável é o evento (baixa aqui, mas impacto alto).

items.q: "Each risk needs a single owner." In this context, the owner is…
options: the person accountable for that risk
items.why: Owner = responsável: a pessoa que responde por aquele risco específico.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de gestão de risco e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "When the strike hit, we pulled the plan off the shelf and acted." This means they…
options: used a response prepared in advance
wrote a brand-new plan on the spot
items.why: Pull off the shelf = usar algo já pronto e guardado para o momento certo.

items.q: "The RH director still has to sign off on the contingency budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new register to all three depots next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two owners agreed the plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Buying more insurance won't move the needle on our response time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
